title: opencode can't reach ollama — provider disabled and models keyed by digest
description:
Blocks every phase of the cross-app harness work: dispatched reviewers and local work-splitting have no backend until this passes.

Two compounding bugs in ~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc:
1. "disabled_providers": ["ollama"] is set while provider.ollama is also fully defined.
2. The provider.ollama.models keys are ollama digest IDs (4eb23ef187e2, 901cae732162, 22130167c4c2, c6eb396dbd59, 359d7dd4bcda) rather than model ids. opencode sends the key as the model id, so ollama/4eb23ef187e2 would 404. Confirmed: those keys match the ID column of 'ollama list' exactly, while GET http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/models returns ids qwen3.8:27b, gemma4:12b, gemma4:e4b, qwen3-vl:8b, qwen3:4b.

Confirmed symptom: 'opencode models' lists only opencode/* zen models, no ollama.

Note OPENCODE_CONFIG merges with the global config rather than replacing it, so a provider disabled globally cannot be re-enabled per project — the fix has to be in the global file.
design: Remove ollama from disabled_providers; re-key provider.ollama.models by the real model ids from /v1/models.
acceptance_criteria: 'opencode models | grep ollama' lists all five models, and a trivial prompt round-trips through ollama/qwen3:4b.
close_reason: Removed ollama from disabled_providers and re-keyed provider.ollama.models by the real /v1/models ids. Verified: 'opencode models | grep ollama' lists all five, and 'opencode run -m ollama/qwen3:4b' round-trips. Backup at ~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc.bak. Marked qwen3-vl:8b with attachment:true so image parts can be sent — whether the shim actually delivers them is still unproven and belongs to the design-reviewer bead.

title: template ships no AGENTS.md — the harness is invisible to every non-Claude agent
description:
harness add installs .claude/** and scripts/**, and leaves AGENTS.md entirely to bd init. Every installed project therefore has an AGENTS.md that is generic beads boilerplate: no review pass, no verify.sh gate, no cold start, no project rules. opencode, Codex, and anything else that reads AGENTS.md gets none of the harness.

Observed in control-center-pro: AGENTS.md is the untouched bd init file from the initial commit while CLAUDE.md carries 266 lines of real instruction. Local opencode agents were working blind.
design: Two distinct files, symmetric pointers, no symlink. AGENTS.md is the agent-agnostic harness contract shipped from template/ (cold start, ledger, gate, review pass, skill locations, local-model lanes, session close, commit style) and owns the single bd managed block. CLAUDE.md is project-specific only and its first line points at AGENTS.md. Claude Code auto-loads CLAUDE.md, opencode auto-loads AGENTS.md; each pointing at the other closes both directions.
acceptance_criteria: template/AGENTS.md exists and is installed by harness add; a fresh install in a non-Claude agent can find the brief, the gate, and the review pass from AGENTS.md alone.
close_reason: template/AGENTS.md ships as the harness contract, installed rather than pasted; add.sh wires CLAUDE.md to import it, collapses bd's three managed blocks to one in AGENTS.md, and strips the bd prime hook bd init re-registers. context.py tracks and counts AGENTS.md and fails on a stray block. Starter dogfooded. Review caught that bd init writes into AGENTS.md too — the first fix created the duplication it was removing, and the gate couldn't see it; also an unbounded sed range and a missing python3 guard. All fixed and verified on fresh installs.

title: harness add must wire the ledger to git — bd init wires neither transport
description:
commands/add.sh runs 'bd init --prefix $prefix' and stops. bd's default .beads/config.yaml ships the export block commented out ('Optional JSONL auto-export ... Disabled by default'), so no .beads/issues.jsonl is ever written. Since .beads/embeddeddolt/ is gitignored, that means every bead a project files lives only in the local Dolt DB and NOTHING about the ledger reaches git. A fresh clone, a second machine, or a teammate gets an empty ledger.

psymail-mini works because its config.yaml was hand-edited three minutes after bd init (metadata.json Aug 10 19:10:42, config.yaml Aug 10 19:13:53) to add:

    sync.remote: "git+https://github.com/bubblesunyum/psymail-mini.git"
    export:
        auto: true

That hand edit is the step the harness extraction never captured. Proof it is the real transport: psymail-mini tracks .beads/issues.jsonl in git (119KB, committed alongside code in 99864ca, 1b57d85, 1f1cdf8...) and 'git ls-remote origin' on psymail-mini shows ONLY HEAD and refs/heads/master — there is no refs/dolt/data. Git is the transport; issues.jsonl is the payload.

Confirmed identical bug in control-center-pro, installed from this starter: diff of the two config.yaml files is exactly those four lines, and CCP had no issues.jsonl at all.
design: Append the block in add.sh right after the successful 'bd init'. sync.remote must be derived from the target's own 'git -C $target remote get-url origin', never hardcoded — psymail-mini's URL is in its config and must not propagate. Handle a repo with no origin yet: write the export block regardless (that is the part that matters for git transport) and skip sync.remote, or leave a clearly marked placeholder. Must stay idempotent — add.sh's contract is that re-running it is safe, so check for an existing 'export:' key before appending.
acceptance_criteria: After 'harness add' on a fresh repo, .beads/config.yaml contains an 'export: auto: true' block and a sync.remote pointing at that project's own git remote; .beads/issues.jsonl is generated and tracked by git. Verified by installing into a scratch repo, filing a bead, and confirming it appears in a committed issues.jsonl.
notes:
TESTED 2026-08-29 in control-center-pro: the Dolt transport works end to end, and it is the better one. Full sequence that was verified:

  bd dolt remote add origin "git+https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git"
  bd dolt commit -m "..."   # 'Nothing to commit' is fine, auto-commit is on
  bd dolt push               # -> creates refs/dolt/data on the GitHub remote

Verified by cloning the repo fresh, running 'bd init --prefix ccp', 'bd dolt remote add origin <url>', 'bd dolt pull'. The clone came back with all 37 issues, both bd remember memories, and full close reasons — WITHOUT the branch commits being pushed at all (origin/main was 4 commits behind). The Dolt ref carries the ledger independently of the branch.

Consequences for add.sh:
1. Writing sync.remote into config.yaml is NOT enough — 'bd dolt remote add' is a separate call and is what actually registers it.
2. A fresh clone does not get the ledger automatically. Onboarding is three commands (bd init / bd dolt remote add / bd dolt pull) and belongs in the starter's docs — see har-sul.
3. bd dolt push creates a visible 'refs/heads/__dolt_remote_info__' branch on the GitHub remote alongside refs/dolt/data. Cosmetic, but surprising in the GitHub branch dropdown; mention it so nobody deletes it.
4. Nothing runs 'bd dolt push' automatically — no beads git hooks are installed by this harness. It has to be in the session-close protocol or a hook, or the ledger silently stops syncing again.

Recommendation: wire BOTH. The jsonl export gives human-readable diffs in git and needs no setup on a clone; the Dolt remote carries memories, history and real merges. They are not exclusive.

title: context.py should measure the real session floor from transcripts, not just count docs
description:
context.py reports what the repo adds to every session — CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md,
the brief, MEMORY.md, skill descriptions — and calls that "tokens every
session". Measured in control-center-pro on 2026-09-01, that line said 4,207
while every real session opened at 53,704. The missing ~50k is Claude Code's
own system prompt, its built-in tool schemas, the skill and agent listings, and
MCP instruction blocks. None of it is readable from a file in the checkout,
which is exactly why a checker that only reads files could not see it and
reported a reassuring number for the wrong quantity.

It IS readable from Claude Code's session transcripts, which record each turn's
usage. They live beside the memory index the script already derives:
~/.claude/projects/<checkout-path-with-slashes-as-dashes>/*.jsonl.

Port from control-center-pro (commit 5606582 / e2af448, scripts/context.py):

- TRANSCRIPTS constant, derived off MEMORY_INDEX.parent.parent
- turn_costs(transcript) — every turn's input+cache_creation+cache_read, with
  zero-cost turns dropped (a resumed session replays its history with no usage
  recorded, and counting those would report a free session floor)
- sessions(limit=12) — recent transcripts, newest last, bounded because the
  floor drifts with Claude Code releases and connector changes
- floor() — median opening context, median not mean so one aborted session
  doesn't move it
- a `floor` line in report(), printing the repo's share inside the measured total
- a `spend` subcommand: per-session turns / open / peak / total in / floor share

The per-session table is the part that pays off, because the two halves of the
bill want opposite fixes. Measured over 16 sessions:

    session   turns    open     peak     total in   floor share
    44b449eb     57  54,884   80,052    3,817,293          82%
    b6e028f0    286  53,621  300,126   55,668,842          28%

A short session is almost entirely floor. A long one is accumulated
conversation and pays ~4x per turn at the end what it paid at the start. One
number could never have said both.

Lands in template/scripts/context.py and the starter's own root copy — see
har-awe on that drift. HARNESS.md changes with it (next bead) or the staleness
gate fires, since context.lock tracks context.py against it.

title: brief.sh surfaces only the seat's Name, discarding the identity it asks for
description:
harness/seat.md's own header says it is 'the seat's identity — the part a session is told about itself at wake-up', and `harness add` instructs the agent to write two or three paragraphs about what the seat is for. scripts/brief.sh:84-86 then extracts only the `**Name:**` line and discards the rest.

Nothing else reads the file — dashboard.py only lists its path. So the Role, the pronouns and every paragraph the installer asked for reach no session, in any tool. The file reads as maintained and has no reader, which is the most expensive kind of doc rot: an agent editing it believes it is changing what future sessions are told, and is not.

Two ways out, both fine, but pick one:
- Emit the paragraphs in the brief. They are ~120 tokens once per session, against a brief that currently costs ~100. That makes the header's claim true.
- Or cut the prose from the template and let seat.md be the Name/Role/Pronouns record brief.sh actually treats it as, with the identity moving into CLAUDE.md where something loads it.

Also worth noting while in there: brief.sh parses `**Name:**` by string prefix, and seat.md is not in HARNESS.md's tracks block, so changing the template's Name format silently degrades every brief to 'unnamed' with nothing failing.
acceptance_criteria: Either the brief carries the seat's identity, or the template stops asking for prose nothing delivers.

title: harness add does not gitignore dashboard/state.json
description:
The starter's own .gitignore has `dashboard/state.json` on line 1. The .gitignore that `harness add` writes into a target project does not — it covers .claude/launch.json and the bd/Dolt files only.

So every installed project immediately shows an untracked dashboard/state.json, and the first agent to run `git add -A` commits it. It is a generated file, rewritten by the dashboard's state thread on every poll, and machine-local — the exact category the launch.json line above it exists to exclude. It also churns the diff of every commit made while the dashboard is running, which is all of them, since the SessionStart and Stop hooks both bring it up.

Seen on a fresh install into /Users/bubbles/dev/bb-kit: state.json appeared in the work tree before any project code existed.

Fix: add the line to whatever template the installer writes, next to .claude/launch.json and with the same kind of comment.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh harness add leaves a clean git status once the dashboard has run.

title: harness add should git init rather than refusing
description:
`harness resolve_target` in commands/lib/install.sh:57 refuses to install into a directory with no .git, telling the user to run 'git init' first. That is a correct diagnosis and an unnecessary stop: every install into a fresh project hits it, and the fix is one command the installer could run itself.

Nothing about `harness add` is meaningful without a repo — it installs a commit-msg hook, and the review packet is built from a diff — so a repo is a dependency of the harness, not a precondition the user is expected to have satisfied. Installing a dependency is what an installer does.

What to build: when the target has no .git, run `git init` as part of add rather than returning 1. Say it happened in the output, in the same voice as the other lines ('initialised the ledger', 'created CLAUDE.md') — 'initialised a git repository' belongs in that list.

Two things to get right:

1. **Only in an empty-of-git directory, and only for the target.** Do not git init somewhere that is inside another repo's working tree — `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` succeeding from the target means it is already tracked by a parent repo, and creating a nested one there is a mess the user did not ask for. In that case the current refusal is the right behavior; keep it, with a message naming the parent repo.
2. **The commit-msg hook needs a first commit to be useful, but do not make one.** Committing on the user's behalf is a bigger liberty than initialising, and an empty repo installs fine — the hook fires on the first real commit either way.
acceptance_criteria: harness add into a fresh directory succeeds and reports the git init. harness add into a subdirectory of an existing repo still refuses, and names the parent.

title: harness add re-appends the bd setup codex block, silently undoing a project's deliberate removal
description:
'harness add' runs 'bd setup codex', which appends a BEGIN/END BEADS CODEX SETUP block to AGENTS.md. The block restates what template/AGENTS.md already says — bd ready / bd show / bd update --claim / bd close, and 'use bd, not markdown TODO lists' — and additionally advertises 'bd prime', which har-am3 removed from the SessionStart hook because the project was paying for it every session.

Two problems:

1. It duplicates always-loaded content. AGENTS.md is loaded every session in both tools, so the block is a permanent token cost for text already on the page above it. ccp's whole ccp-veh session was about getting that number down (4148 -> 3798); this puts some of it back.

2. It is silent and it recurs. A project that deliberately removes the block gets it re-appended by the next 'harness add' with no mention in the output — 'add' reports what it installs, not what bd appended afterward. ccp hit this today: AGENTS.md came back modified from a run whose purpose was installing one missing script, and it was only caught because the diff was read line by line. HARNESS.md acknowledges the block exists (the drift check normalises it away) but nothing stops it being re-added.

FIX, roughly in order of preference:
  a. Don't run 'bd setup codex' from 'harness add' at all — template/AGENTS.md already carries the contract, in better words. Codex hook setup, if it is wanted, is a separate opt-in.
  b. Run it only when AGENTS.md does not exist yet, so a fresh install gets it and an existing project is never rewritten.
  c. At minimum, say so in the output: 'bd setup codex appended a block to AGENTS.md'.

(a) is the honest one: the block's content is a worse duplicate of what the template already installs.

Filed from control-center-pro, which reverts this by hand on every 'harness add' (see ccp commit 01a6848).

title: commit-msg advertises its own bypass — drop the --no-verify line
description:
template/scripts/hooks/commit-msg ends the 'this commit names no bead' message with:

    Genuinely unfilable? git commit --no-verify

The hook exists to keep every commit linked to the work it came from. Printing the bypass in the same breath as the rule undercuts it: the escape hatch is the path of least resistance at exactly the moment someone is being asked to spend a line filing a bead, and an agent reading that message will take it. A rule the enforcer offers to waive is a convention, not a gate.

Filed from control-center-pro, which removed the line locally (ccp commit 01a6848) and now diverges from the template permanently — 'harness update' reports scripts/hooks/commit-msg as drifted forever, which is exactly the false alarm the contract-file check is supposed to avoid.

FIX: delete the two lines from template/scripts/hooks/commit-msg. --no-verify keeps working for anyone who genuinely needs it; git documents it. The hook does not have to.

Note ccp records the reason in a comment above the 'if [ -z "$ids" ]' block. If the template drops the line, that comment can go too and ccp's copy returns to matching.

title: opencode 1.18.25 lists a random subset of project skills
description:
`opencode debug skill` returns a different random subset of the project's
.claude/skills/ on every run — measured five runs in a row in this repo and in a
fresh probe install, each surfacing one to three of agentic-review, beads,
handoff, workflow. The seven global skills (~/.claude/skills, ~/.agents/skills)
come back complete every time; only the project-scoped scan races.

Not fixable from the harness. Ruled out by experiment:
  • `skills.paths: [".claude/skills"]` in opencode.json — same race.
  • Copying the skills to `.opencode/skills/` — same race.
So it is not about where they live or how they are registered.

What is unproven: whether the session's own skill loader shares the bug or only
`debug skill` does. Proving that needs an authenticated provider, which this
machine does not have. If it does share it, har-gdz's "can invoke the workflow
skill by name" is only sometimes true under opencode, and the fix is upstream.

Next: reproduce against a newer opencode, then file it at sst/opencode with the
five-run transcript.

title: review.sh must refuse a packet larger than the reviewing model's context
description:
A local reviewer will silently receive a truncated packet and report confidently on the first few thousand tokens. The review appears to run and appears to pass — the worst available outcome for a gate.

OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH is unset on this machine and the ollama server default is 4096-8192 tokens depending on build. qwen3.8:27b advertises context length 262144, but that is the architecture maximum, not what the server allocates. The OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions endpoint has no num_ctx field, so opencode cannot raise it per request. Meanwhile review.sh only warns above 3000 lines — roughly 45k tokens.
design: Give each role in the roster (har-ctd) a context budget. review.sh refuses rather than warns when the packet exceeds the budget of the role about to read it, and says which earlier commit to review from instead. Set OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH in the launchd environment. Measure the real KV cost of a 27B at a usable context on this machine before promising it as the correctness reviewer.
acceptance_criteria: A packet over the target role's budget exits non-zero with the narrower command to run; no reviewer is ever handed a packet it cannot read whole.

title: scripts/agent.sh — run a harness role on whichever model is configured for it
description:
The second half of the reviewer work: once the prompt bodies are extracted (har-wkr), something has to run them somewhere. Today model choice is hard-coded in .claude/agents frontmatter, which no other tool can read.

Running review off the account is the point — the packet never enters the calling session's context, and a local model reads it for free. Note the Claude path is off-context, not off-account: 'claude -p' uses the same quota, and the child inherits the project's .claude/settings.json, so SessionStart hooks fire on every spawn. Pass --settings with empty hooks or each reviewer costs more than the native subagent it replaces.
design:
scripts/agent.sh <role> <prompt> <context...>: resolve role to model via the roster (har-ctd), run it — ollama, claude -p, or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint — and print findings. scripts/reviewer.sh becomes a thin caller; the agentic-review skill calls the script rather than spawning natively.

Local models will not produce ReportFindings-shaped output, so define a plain-markdown finding format and check they hit it reliably.
acceptance_criteria: The full review pass runs from a bare shell with no Claude Code present and produces findings in the same format it does inside Claude Code.

title: harness update — deliver harness fixes to existing installs, loudly for contract files
description:
har-whx.4 scopes an update to the dashboard only, and says explicitly that overwriting other harness files in an existing project needs a guided process of its own. This is that process.

The gap it closes: commands/add.sh:98 never overwrites, so a file that exists in the target prints 'skip (already there)'. That is the right default, and it is what makes re-running add safe. But it also means no fix ever reaches a project that already has the file. Once template/AGENTS.md exists (har-32s), every existing install will see an AGENTS.md — the bd init boilerplate — skip it, and keep the broken one. The skip line scrolls past among other skip lines and nothing says the install didn't take.

control-center-pro only survives this because a session was present to apply the fix by hand.
design:
Name a set of contract files — AGENTS.md, opencode.json, the generated .opencode/agent and .claude/agents — where 'exists but differs from the template' is a loud warning rather than a quiet skip:

  ⚠ AGENTS.md exists and differs from the template
    the harness contract is not installed — diff and merge it

Still never overwrites; it just stops being silent about the one category of file where silence means the install failed.

Pair it with an update/--diff mode listing every target file that differs from its template source. That also catches the root-vs-template drift in the starter itself (har-yp3) — .claude/settings.json and AGENTS.md have both diverged there.
acceptance_criteria: Running against an install with stale contract files reports each one by name and exits non-zero; ordinary files still skip quietly.
notes: This is now what gates the opencode rollout to control-center-pro. It has an older install: 'harness add' would drop in opencode.json and scripts/opencode-agents.py (both new files, so the never-overwrite rule lets them through) but would leave its verify.sh without the drift check, its review.sh scope without *.json, and its HARNESS.md without the opencode section. Those three are exactly the contract-file case this bead is about.
close_reason: harness update ships as a command, and add.sh now warns loudly instead of skipping quietly for contract files. Classification is read off the template's content — a '── FILL THIS IN' block means the project is meant to edit it (verify.sh, the reviewers, seat.md, dashboard.py), everything else is contract and exits non-zero when stale OR missing entirely, which is control-center-pro's absent opencode.json. Comparison normalises the installer's own post-copy edits (bd setup codex's AGENTS.md block, the tidier's json.dumps key reorder) or every fresh install read as stale; a gate step now holds that. Shared logic between add and update lives in commands/lib/install.sh. Dogfooding caught two bugs before review: the false-alarm-on-fresh-install, and the classifier grepping bare words so HARNESS.md demoted itself the moment it documented the rule. Both reviewers independently found only issues already fixed. Starter's own root drift filed as har-awe.

title: stop paying for bd prime — remove the SessionStart hook bd setup claude installs
description:
HARNESS.md states the stock beads SessionStart hook is replaced by scripts/brief.sh. It is not replaced — both run. .claude/settings.json in harness-starter and in control-center-pro each carry a second SessionStart entry, 'bd prime --hook-json', written by bd setup claude, alongside 'scripts/brief.sh --hook'.

Measured in ccp: brief.sh --hook is 1072 bytes (~236 tokens); bd prime --hook-json is 7949 bytes (~1900 tokens). Real per-session load is ~5900 tokens while context.py reports 4022, because it counts docs and not hook output. The harness's headline saving is currently negative and its own budget line understates by about a third.

bd prime's bulk is a command reference and session-close protocol — the same ground the beads skill (80 lines) covers on demand. Paying for it always-loaded is what progressive disclosure exists to avoid.

Nothing is lost by removing it: brief.sh already prints seat, ledger counts, ready work and memory keys, and the beads skill carries the command surface.
design:
Remove the second SessionStart entry from .claude/settings.json in both repos and in template/.claude/settings.json.

bd setup claude will re-add it, so documentation alone will not hold. Document the override loudly in HARNESS.md and README — why the built-in step is overridden and that the harness config must be re-applied after any bd setup claude — and back it with a verify.sh check so a silent regression fails the gate.

Teach context.py to count SessionStart hook output, not just docs; otherwise the budget line keeps lying about what a session actually pays.
acceptance_criteria: No bd prime hook in either repo or the template. verify.sh fails when one reappears. context.py's cost line includes hook output. HARNESS.md and README state the override and the re-apply rule.
close_reason: Removed the bd prime SessionStart hook from harness-starter and control-center-pro (template was already clean). Added a foreign-hook check to context.py covering all three settings files Claude Code merges, documented the override in HARNESS.md and README. Review found the check only read the project settings file — bd setup claude --global writes the same hook to ~/.claude/settings.json — plus a fail-open on malformed JSON and an empty-command false positive; all three fixed and verified.

title: make opencode load the harness — instructions, generated agents, no symlinks
description:
Verified against the installed opencode binary rather than assumed:

- opencode ALREADY discovers project .claude/skills/ natively — 'opencode debug skill' finds workflow, beads and handoff with no .opencode/ directory present, and the binary carries OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE_SKILLS, so it is deliberate. No skills symlink is needed; don't add one.
- opencode does NOT read .claude/agents/, and symlinking it is worse than leaving it: the frontmatter loads but corrupts. Claude's 'model: haiku' parses as provider 'haiku' with an empty model id, the comma-string 'tools:' resolves to invalid, and 'mode: all' puts each reviewer in the primary agent picker. It looks like it worked and fails at spawn.
- opencode has no plugin hook that can inject context at session start — the hook names are event, chat.message, chat.params, chat.headers, chat.completion, tool.execute.before/after, auth, config, permission.*. The 'event' hook is a notification sink with no return channel. Do not build the plugin the earlier plan called for.
- It does have a declarative 'instructions' config key, documented in the binary's own customize-opencode skill.
design:
Ship template/opencode.json with instructions: ["AGENTS.md", ".claude/HARNESS.md"]. Generate .opencode/agent/*.md from the same reviewer prompt bodies as .claude/agents/*.md — two frontmatter dialects, one source, never a symlink. Keep AGENTS.md's 'run scripts/brief.sh yourself' line as the fallback for the dynamic half, which no static instructions file can carry.

Explicitly: no .opencode/skill symlink, and no session-start plugin.
acceptance_criteria: An opencode session in a fresh install loads AGENTS.md automatically, can invoke the workflow skill by name, and can spawn a reviewer that actually resolves its model.
close_reason: opencode.json declares AGENTS.md + CLAUDE.md as instructions, scripts/opencode-agents.py generates .opencode/agent/*.md from .claude/agents/*.md, add.sh runs it at install and verify.sh fails on drift. No skills symlink, no session-start plugin, no symlinked agents. Verified against opencode 1.18.25: all four agents resolve with mode subagent and the right tool denials, config resolves, a probe install into a fresh repo produces the lot. Two deviations from the design, both noted in .claude/HARNESS.md — instructions lists CLAUDE.md rather than .claude/HARNESS.md so opencode always-loads exactly what Claude Code does, and the generated agents carry no model: line (har-ctd). Skill discovery turns out to be racy in opencode itself: har-nvb.

title: no model roster — nothing says which model plays which role, and nothing asks
description: The harness hard-codes model choice in .claude/agents frontmatter (haiku, sonnet). That is unreadable to any other tool, unconfigurable per machine, and wrong the moment someone has local models worth using. Roles beyond review — librarian, summarization, implementing an already-specced bead — have no notion of model at all.
design: harness/models.json maps roles to models. Machine-local and gitignored, because it names models the machine happens to have. Missing on first run: detect available backends (ollama list, claude on PATH, opencode's configured providers), prompt the user for a model per role, write the file. Roles cover more than reviewers.
acceptance_criteria: First review on a fresh clone prompts for models and writes harness/models.json; subsequent runs are silent.
notes: har-gdz landed the opencode side with no model: at all — Claude's tier aliases (haiku, sonnet) don't exist there, it wants a provider-qualified id, and which provider an install has authenticated isn't knowable from the starter. So .opencode/agent/*.md inherit the session's model and reviewer-taste stops being the cheap one under opencode. The roster this bead builds is what scripts/opencode-agents.py needs to emit a real model line.

title: extract the reviewer prompts and generate both agent dialects
description:
scripts/review.sh already produces a packet any model can read — the packet is portable, the spawn is not. The reviewers are .claude/agents/*.md with Claude-specific frontmatter, so the standing review pass cannot run in opencode at all.

Confirmed the naive fix is a trap: symlinking .claude/agents into .opencode/agent loads, but 'model: haiku' parses as provider 'haiku' with an empty model id and the comma-string 'tools:' resolves to invalid. It fails at spawn, not at load.

This is the half that unblocks opencode reviewers. The dispatcher that runs them on a chosen model is separate.
design: Move the prompt bodies to scripts/reviewers/{taste,correctness,design}.md — no frontmatter, single source of truth. Generate .claude/agents/*.md and .opencode/agent/*.md from them, each in its own dialect, so the two can't drift and neither is a symlink.
acceptance_criteria: Both dialects generate from one body; an opencode session can spawn reviewer-taste and it resolves its model.
notes: har-gdz delivered most of this: scripts/opencode-agents.py generates .opencode/agent/*.md from .claude/agents/*.md, and scripts/verify.sh fails when they drift. Difference from the design above — the single source is .claude/agents/ itself rather than a new frontmatter-free scripts/reviewers/, so only one dialect is generated instead of two. Same guarantee, one fewer moving part; a third tool would be the reason to revisit it. What's left here is the model half, which is har-ctd: the generated agents carry no model: line yet.

title: drop the duplicate beads block from CLAUDE.md and guard against a second one
description:
Verified on a scratch repo: bd setup is non-destructive. It appends its marker-delimited block and leaves hand-authored content above and below intact across re-runs. So there is no ownership fight — bd owns its markers, the harness owns the rest of AGENTS.md, and template/AGENTS.md can be hand-authored around the block.

What remains is a plain duplicate. ccp has three copies of the same guidance across two files: CLAUDE.md:5-58 and AGENTS.md:50-103 are byte-identical (both hash:6cd5cc61), plus AGENTS.md:105-127 from the codex recipe. harness-starter's CLAUDE.md has no block at all, so the two repos already diverge. The CLAUDE.md copy is 53 lines of always-loaded budget buying nothing.
design:
Keep the codex recipe's block in AGENTS.md — it is clean in both repos and it is the AGENTS.md-native one. Remove the CLAUDE.md copy. Careful: the claude recipe bundles the CLAUDE.md section and the SessionStart hook, so test --remove on a copy first; the hook it installed is the duplicate bd prime covered by its own bead.

Do not run bd setup opencode: it is additive, not a replacement, and appends a second 128-line profile:full block on top of the codex one.

Guard it with a verify.sh check rather than trusting the policy to hold.
acceptance_criteria: Exactly one BEGIN BEADS block in the repo, in AGENTS.md. verify.sh fails on a second block or on any block in CLAUDE.md.
close_reason: template/AGENTS.md ships as the harness contract, installed rather than pasted; add.sh wires CLAUDE.md to import it, collapses bd's three managed blocks to one in AGENTS.md, and strips the bd prime hook bd init re-registers. context.py tracks and counts AGENTS.md and fails on a stray block. Starter dogfooded. Review caught that bd init writes into AGENTS.md too — the first fix created the duplication it was removing, and the gate couldn't see it; also an unbounded sed range and a missing python3 guard. All fixed and verified on fresh installs.

title: CLAUDE.snippet.md is a manual paste-and-delete step
description:
template/CLAUDE.snippet.md instructs a human or agent to paste three sections into the project's CLAUDE.md and then delete the file. An install is only as correct as someone remembering to do that, and the failure is silent.

This is the proximate cause of the AGENTS.md gap: in control-center-pro the snippet reached CLAUDE.md and nothing ever reached AGENTS.md.
design: The snippet's content becomes part of template/AGENTS.md, installed by harness add like every other file. Nothing is pasted by hand.
acceptance_criteria: CLAUDE.snippet.md is gone from template/; its content is installed automatically.
close_reason: template/AGENTS.md ships as the harness contract, installed rather than pasted; add.sh wires CLAUDE.md to import it, collapses bd's three managed blocks to one in AGENTS.md, and strips the bd prime hook bd init re-registers. context.py tracks and counts AGENTS.md and fails on a stray block. Starter dogfooded. Review caught that bd init writes into AGENTS.md too — the first fix created the duplication it was removing, and the gate couldn't see it; also an unbounded sed range and a missing python3 guard. All fixed and verified on fresh installs.

title: session close must push the ledger — nothing runs bd dolt push automatically
description:
The Dolt transport works (see har-nqi, tested), but it is entirely manual. This harness installs no beads git hooks — .git/hooks/ in both psymail-mini and control-center-pro contains at most the harness's own commit-msg shim, and beads' pre-push hook (which would sync on git push) is never installed. add.sh:154 deliberately avoids .git/hooks because beads rewrites that directory on upgrade.

So a session can file beads, close beads, commit, git push, and leave the Dolt ledger a full session behind, with no signal that it happened. That is the same class of silent drift as har-nqi, just one layer up.

psymail-mini is the live proof: sync.remote has been configured there since Aug 10 with a registered Dolt remote, and 'git ls-remote origin' still shows no refs/dolt/data. Correctly configured, never pushed, for three weeks.
design: Cheapest honest option is a check rather than an action: have the brief or verify.sh compare the local Dolt commit against the remote ref and print one line when they differ. Pushing on the user's behalf at session close is a bigger call and should stay opt-in — the repo profile is conservative about outward-facing actions by default.
acceptance_criteria: A session cannot end with an unpushed ledger without being told. Either the session-close protocol in CLAUDE.snippet names 'bd dolt push' explicitly, or the harness runs it, or verify.sh reports the ledger as ahead of its remote.
notes: Depends on har-nqi landing the remote registration first.

title: bd remember memories never reach git — the export omits them by design
description:
The JSONL export that carries the ledger to git contains only issues. Memories written with 'bd remember' — the ones the session brief surfaces every session as 'known traps' — stay in the local Dolt DB and reach no clone.

Measured in control-center-pro:
  grep _type .beads/issues.jsonl  ->  37 "_type":"issue", 0 memory records
  bd export --all -o /tmp/all.jsonl  ->  37 issue + 2 memory records
  .beads/export-state.json literally reads {"issues":37,"memories":0}

Both of CCP's memories are real load-bearing knowledge (the Permissions.swift 1336-error trap, the SwiftUI-import undercount) and neither is in git.

The export config block bd init ships exposes auto/path/interval/git-add — no option to include memories. So this is not a setting that was missed; the auto-export path cannot carry them.

This matters more for the harness than for beads generally: CLAUDE.snippet tells every project 'Use bd remember for persistent knowledge — do NOT use MEMORY.md files'. The harness actively directs knowledge into the one store that does not survive a clone.
design: 'bd export --all -o .beads/issues.jsonl' would carry both, but check whether bd import round-trips memory records before adopting it — a file the auto-export then overwrites with an issues-only version would silently drop them again. A separate tracked .beads/memories.jsonl may be safer since auto-export owns issues.jsonl.
acceptance_criteria: Either memories ride to git (an explicit 'bd export --all' step writing a tracked file), or the harness stops telling projects that bd remember is durable and says plainly that memories are machine-local.
notes: Resolved differently than this bead assumed: memories DO survive if the Dolt transport is used. Verified by clone in har-nqi — 'bd dolt pull' into a fresh clone returned both of control-center-pro's memories. The JSONL export still omits them, so this bead now reads: if a project relies on the jsonl export alone, bd remember is machine-local and CLAUDE.snippet's 'use bd remember for persistent knowledge' is false for it. Wiring the Dolt remote (har-nqi) is the fix; this bead is the docs/telling-the-truth half.

title: bd export is incremental — a stale issues.jsonl can be committed without anyone noticing
description:
With 'export: auto: true' set, .beads/issues.jsonl is not written synchronously on every bd mutation. Measured in control-center-pro: filing a bead left issues.jsonl byte-identical; a following 'bd export' still did not contain it (export-state.json carries a last_dolt_commit high-water mark and only emits what has advanced past it); a second 'bd export' picked it up. Deleting a bead is worse — the deleted issue stayed in issues.jsonl through repeated 'bd export' runs, and only a full regeneration (rm .beads/issues.jsonl .beads/export-state.json && bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl) produced a correct file.

Consequence: a session can close beads, commit, and push a issues.jsonl that is missing the closes or still lists deleted work. The ledger silently disagrees with itself across machines, which is the exact failure the ledger exists to prevent.
design: Cheapest correct option is a full regeneration rather than an incremental export, since the file is small (43KB / 37 issues in CCP, 120KB in psymail-mini) and incremental export demonstrably does not handle deletes. A pre-commit hook is the natural home, but note scripts/hooks/ is the harness's own directory — .beads/hooks/ is managed by beads and gets rewritten on upgrade, and add.sh already comments on that trap at line 154. Alternative: fold it into verify.sh so the gate fails on a stale export.
acceptance_criteria: The harness guarantees a fresh, correct issues.jsonl reaches every commit that touches the ledger — via a pre-commit step, a verify.sh check, or an explicit step in the session-close protocol. Verified by deleting a bead and confirming the committed issues.jsonl no longer contains it.
notes:
Refined after reading the config schema in .beads/config.yaml (the commented block bd init ships). The export block supports more than 'auto':

    export:
      auto: false
      path: issues.jsonl
      interval: 60s
      git-add: false

'interval: 60s' explains the lag measured in control-center-pro — auto-export is a timer, not a per-mutation write, so a bead filed and committed inside the same minute misses the export. The original framing (high-water mark alone) was incomplete: it is a 60s timer AND incremental semantics that does not drop deleted issues.

'git-add: true' is likely the cheapest half of the fix — it stages issues.jsonl automatically so a session cannot forget it. Neither psymail-mini nor CCP sets it. That still leaves deletes needing a full regen.

Separately: the export block exposes no option to include memories, and the default export omits them — see har-jx2.

Blocked by har-nqi.

title: dashboard: a dropped poll blanks the whole repaint
description: tick() in dashboard/index.html wraps the fetch AND all ten draw calls in one try. A single dropped fetch jumps to the catch, paints the pulse offline, and skips the entire repaint, so the board silently keeps whatever it last drew — which is what 'the dashboard stopped showing new beads and commits' looks like from outside. Split the fetch out of the draw try/catch: a transient fetch failure should touch the pulse indicator and nothing else. Keeping the last good payload and redrawing from it would be better still. Diagnosed in control-center-pro as ccp-not; the code is this starter's.
notes: Overlaps work in flight: har-whx.1 added 'runStates = d.runs || {}' as the first line inside tick()'s try, before drawRuns(). When the fetch is split out, that assignment belongs with the fetch's success path, not with the draws — every run button on the page is drawn from it.
close_reason: tick() catches the fetch and the repaint apart; board survives a dropped poll, draw failures say so distinctly. e036fa4

title: dashboard falls behind its own polling
description: Diagnosed in control-center-pro (bead ccp-not), but the code is this starter's, so every install has it. state() takes 2.5-3.1s to build while CACHE_TTL is 4.0s and the page polls every 2500ms, so the cache expires between polls and the server regenerates on roughly every other request — a ~75% duty cycle of continuous bd and git shell-outs. Each miss holds _lock, so a poll landing inside a generation blocks up to 3s; on a 2.5s cadence responses back up until the browser drops the connection, leaving BrokenPipeError in the dash log. Agent bd commands in a terminal make it worse: the dashboard's own bd calls contend with them on the embedded Dolt lock, so generation slows exactly when the ledger is changing. Of the 2.5-3.1s, ledger_state is ~0.88s across three bd shell-outs (bd ready, bd list --all --limit 0, bd stale --days 14), each spinning up its own Dolt engine.
design: Regenerate on a background timer and serve the last snapshot immediately, so do_GET never blocks. That removes the collision rather than retuning it. If on-demand generation is kept instead, CACHE_TTL has to exceed the poll interval by more than one generation cost — better, derive it from how long the last generation actually took.
acceptance_criteria: Eight curls two seconds apart all return fast, with no alternating multi-second spikes. A burst of bd commands in a terminal leaves the pulse live and the board tracking. No BrokenPipeError in the dash log.
close_reason: refresher() thread owns the build; requests read the last finished snapshot. budget() on a 60s clock (1.75s of a 3.2s build). shot warms state before Chrome. Responses 1-3ms, builds 1.1s, no BrokenPipeError. a89d0ce

title: dashboard gate reads every passing step as failed
description: verify_state() in scripts/dashboard.py decides a step passed with: ok = bool(text.strip()) and not re.search(r'\\berror:', text). But step() in scripts/verify.sh writes the command's output to the log and a passing step produces an EMPTY log, so bool(text.strip()) is False and every green step is read as failed. Result: scripts/verify.sh prints 'verify: passed' and the dashboard header says 'failing' with all steps red, permanently. Confirmed 2026-08-29: run state 'ok' and gate status 'failed' in the same state.json. The empty-log guard exists to stop a step that never ran from reading green, so the fix is not to drop it — verify.sh knows each step's exit status and should record it (a per-step status file next to the log), with the text heuristic as the fallback for projects whose tools print a verdict.
acceptance_criteria: A passing scripts/verify.sh leaves the dashboard header reading 'verified'. A step that never ran still does not read as passed.

title: review packet can't see the dashboard page
description: SCOPE in scripts/review.sh:47 lists '*.py' '*.sh' '*.md' and some paths, but not '*.html'. dashboard/index.html is the largest file in the project and where most dashboard work lands, and no reviewer has ever seen a line of it. Same class as the bug the comment right above SCOPE describes for bin/ and commands/. dashboard/vendor/* is already excluded, so adding '*.html' picks up the page and nothing else.
close_reason: *.html added to SCOPE in both copies; HARNESS.md and the agentic-review skill updated to match. 6639e73

title: harness add ships untracked junk from template/
description: commands/add.sh:113 lists files with 'find $TEMPLATE -type f', which ignores .gitignore. A working starter checkout that has run the dashboard has template/scripts/__pycache__/*.pyc, so the installer tries to sed a binary file. Under LC_CTYPE=C.UTF-8 — which every Python parent sets, including the dashboard's own verify button — BSD sed fails with 'RE error: illegal byte sequence', and add.sh dies partway through the copy leaving a half-installed project. From a plain terminal (locale unset) sed is byte-wise and it passes, so the gate is green by hand and red from the dashboard. Fix: source the file list from git (tracked + untracked-not-ignored), so the product is what the repo says it is.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/verify.sh passes under LC_CTYPE=C.UTF-8. A .pyc in template/scripts/__pycache__ is never installed.
close_reason: File list from git ls-files, plus an up-front check that every listed file is on disk. ce68237

title: harness update dashboard
description: A dashboard-scoped update, deliberately NOT a whole-harness update: overwriting other harness files in an existing project needs a guided process of its own. Re-copies dashboard/ and scripts/dashboard.py from the starter checkout, never touches dashboard.toml. harness add stays never-overwrite (commands/add.sh:98). Also fixes the self-hosting drift README calls out at README.md:105 for these files.
notes: The 'guided process of its own' this description defers to is now filed separately — see the harness update bead.

title: dashboard: run table to dashboard.toml, project/prefix at runtime
description: Move the run table out of dashboard.py into a dashboard.toml the update never touches (tomllib, stdlib). Move {{PROJECT}}/{{PREFIX}} install-time substitution to runtime lookup so shipped files are byte-identical everywhere.

title: dashboard: one run-button table, server-side
description: The run buttons are configured in four places that must agree: TASKS in scripts/dashboard.py (commands), const TASKS + RUN_LABEL in dashboard/index.html (header strip), a hardcoded push button in the staging lane, and a hardcoded verify button in the gate pane. Collapse to one server-side table carrying command, label, busy label and placement; the page renders slots from d.runs and names no task.
acceptance_criteria: Adding a run button means editing TASKS in dashboard.py only. No task key appears in index.html.
close_reason: One server-side TASKS table carries command, label, busy and placement; page renders slots via runButton/runSlot and names no task. c04e698

title: workflow skill: rewrite token discipline around the measured floor and the subagent asymmetry
description:
The token-discipline section argues from first principles about a single
account. Now that har-a67 makes the floor measurable, it can argue from
numbers, and two of its rules change shape.

Add the floor/conversation split as the section's opening frame: a session
opens at ~54k before it has done anything, that context is re-sent every turn,
and in a 60-turn session it is ~80% of the bill — but past a hundred turns
accumulated conversation takes over and the worst measured session reached 300k
paying ~4x per turn what it paid at the start. Everything read into the main
window is paid for again on every turn that follows, so WHERE a read lands
matters more than how big it is. Point at `context.py spend`.

Sharpen "subagents are for fan-out, not delegation theater" with the asymmetry
that makes it concrete: a search that opens eight files costs the main window
~30k for the rest of the session; the same search in an Explore subagent costs
its summary, once.

And settle the question this audit was started to answer, because every project
running this harness will ask it: the review pass is not where the tokens go.
Measured across 16 sessions in control-center-pro, every reviewer ever spawned
returned ~15k tokens in total — roughly 1% of what a single working session
spends, and a typical three-commit packet is 42KB read once and discarded.
Reviewers are the cheapest thing in the harness. The expensive habit is reading
the repo into your own window. A starter whose standing review pass looks
extravagant will get switched off by the first person trying to economise, and
they will have cut the wrong thing.

Wording landed in control-center-pro (commits 5606582 and b7fd801,
.claude/skills/workflow/SKILL.md). Lands in template/ and the starter's own
root — see har-awe.

title: HARNESS.md should explain why the session floor is measured from transcripts, not counted from files
description:
Companion to har-a67 — they must land together, because context.lock tracks
scripts/context.py against .claude/HARNESS.md and the staleness gate fires
otherwise.

HARNESS.md currently describes the cost line as "what a session pays before it
does anything", which is what the line claims and not what it measures. Add the
correction, in the section that already explains why the count includes
AGENTS.md as well as CLAUDE.md. The reasoning is the durable part: the count
measures what the repo adds, was quietly reassuring about the wrong number, and
the thing it could not see was invisible precisely because it isn't a file.

Wording landed in control-center-pro (commit 5606582, .claude/HARNESS.md) —
port it, generalising the CCP-specific figures to "measured on one project".

Also worth stating there: the floor is worth measuring and mostly not worth
fighting. Deferred tool schemas already do the heavy lifting — a connector with
42 tools costs ~230 tokens of bare names, not thousands. The controllable slice
is ~5k of skill listing, agent listing and MCP instruction blocks; the other
~44k is Claude Code's own prompt and built-in tools and no edit to a harness
touches it. A starter that sends people hunting the floor sends them after 5k
while the session-length problem is worth ten times that.

title: opencode: beads skills should prefer scripts/brief.sh (≈200 tokens) over bd prime (≈1900) for session start
notes: Both template beads skills (.claude/skills/beads/SKILL.md and .agents/skills/beads/SKILL.md) said First Step: bd prime (≈1900 tokens). In this harness scripts/brief.sh is the session start (≈200 tokens) and workflow skill says it replaces bd prime. Opencode debug skill showed beads resolved from .agents in normal mode and .claude in --pure, so both locations need same note. Fix: add 'In this harness scripts/brief.sh is the session start — prefer it over bd prime which is generic fallback.' Applied to both files in control-center-pro.

title: opencode: make AGENTS.md brief callout unmissable for opencode (first action is bash scripts/brief.sh)
notes: AGENTS.md Start-with-brief section buried opencode fallback in a sentence (if your tool didn't hand it to you, run it yourself). Claude gets brief via SessionStart hook; opencode has no equivalent hook (HARNESS.md:84 — event/chat.message have no return channel), so every opencode session started blind and rediscovered ledger. Fix applied in control-center-pro: added blockquote '> opencode: your first action every session is bash scripts/brief.sh — ... you must run it yourself before anything else.' Template AGENTS.md should ship this callout so future installs don't regress.

title: opencode: agentic-review skill should document opencode reviewer spawn (.opencode/agent/ vs Task)
notes: template/.claude/skills/agentic-review/SKILL.md said spawn all three reviewers in parallel via Task subagents — Claude-only phrasing. Opencode reviewers live in .opencode/agent/ (generated by scripts/opencode-agents.py) and are spawned via opencode's agent system, not Task. Both discover .claude/skills/ and packet is same, only spawn tool differs. Fix: add 'In Claude Code spawn via Task; in opencode spawn same three agents from .opencode/agent/ in parallel.' Keeps skill tool-agnostic while giving opencode sessions a concrete command.

title: opencode: consolidate opencode.json to single root file — plugin belongs in template/opencode.json, not .opencode/opencode.json or tui.json
notes: Found in control-center-pro: root opencode.json had instructions only, .opencode/opencode.json had instructions+plugin, .opencode/tui.json had plugin. Opencode merges both project configs so it appeared to work, but harness_is_contract only tracked root file — plugin drift was invisible and split-brain hid the real source. Fix: template/opencode.json should be single source of truth (instructions + plugin). Add harness update check that warns if .opencode/opencode.json duplicates instructions/plugin, and document that tui.json must not carry plugin. Reference fix commit 452eb36 in control-center-pro.

title: harness add should merge instructions into .opencode/opencode.json so opencode loads AGENTS.md
description:
In control-center-pro the plugin install created .opencode/opencode.json with only {"plugin": ["opencode-stats-for-nerds"]}, shadowing the committed root opencode.json that carries {"instructions": ["AGENTS.md", "CLAUDE.md"]}. Opencode prefers .opencode/opencode.json, so it never loaded AGENTS.md — the review harness (scripts/review.sh + reviewer-taste/correctness/design) was invisible to opencode.

What was done to fix control-center-pro: merged instructions into .opencode/opencode.json:

{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "instructions": ["AGENTS.md", "CLAUDE.md"],
  "plugin": ["opencode-stats-for-nerds"]
}

harness add should do the same when it wires opencode: if .opencode/opencode.json exists, merge missing instructions/plugin entries rather than creating a plugin-only file that shadows the root config. Also ensure the template and the add/update path never leaves a .opencode/opencode.json without instructions.

title: two copies of the beads skill, and each tool reads a different one
description:
After `harness add`, a project has the beads skill twice: .claude/skills/beads/SKILL.md and .agents/skills/beads/SKILL.md. They are byte-identical at install time.

Claude Code resolves the .claude/ copy. opencode resolves the .agents/ copy — confirmed with `opencode debug skill` on opencode 1.18.25, which lists 'beads → .agents/skills/beads/SKILL.md' while resolving workflow, handoff and agentic-review from .claude/skills/.

So the two tools read different files under one name, nothing compares them, and the gate does not check either. Edit one and the other tool keeps the old guidance with no signal. This is the same class of drift that scripts/opencode-agents.py exists to prevent for the reviewers, left unhandled for this one skill.

Worth deciding which it is: if bd owns .agents/skills/beads, the harness should not also ship .claude/skills/beads and should let both tools find bd's copy. If the harness owns it, the .agents/ copy should be generated or checked the way the opencode agents are. Either is fine; two unmanaged copies is not.
acceptance_criteria: One source of truth, or a gate check that fails when the copies diverge.

title: the starter's own root has drifted from template/ — three contract files
description:
`harness update` (har-sgq) reports three contract files in this repo's root that differ from the file in template/ they were installed from:

  .claude/HARNESS.md
  .claude/skills/agentic-review/SKILL.md
  scripts/review.sh

Each is a real improvement made to the running copy and never carried back — exactly the trap README's 'Working on the starter' warns about. The root copy is what runs here, so the fixes work; every project installed from this starter gets the old version.

Run 'harness update --diff .' for the content. Merging is by hand on purpose: the direction is root → template, which is the opposite of the direction the tool assumes, so read each hunk before moving it.

title: dashboard/state.json is tracked and rewritten every session
description:
git ls-files confirms dashboard/state.json is tracked, and it is dirty in every harnessed checkout right now. It is rewritten as the dashboard runs, so it shows up as a diff at the end of every session, and two concurrent sessions in one checkout both write it.

.claude/launch.json has exactly this problem and add.sh already gitignores it for exactly this reason — the same treatment was never applied to the second file that needs it.
design: Gitignore it the way add.sh already ignores .claude/launch.json, or make it per-session. Whichever, it should stop appearing in unrelated diffs.
acceptance_criteria: A session that runs the dashboard leaves no dashboard/state.json diff behind.

title: /tmp paths collide when two apps work the same checkout
description:
Every harness scratch path is namespaced by project prefix but not by session: brief.sh's /tmp/.PREFIX-ready.json, review.sh's /tmp/PREFIX-review-packet.md, context.py's /tmp/PREFIX-knowledge-digest.md, verify.sh's /tmp/PREFIX-verify.

Two concurrent sessions in one checkout — a Claude Code session and an opencode session, which is the exact scenario this whole cross-app effort is built for — overwrite each other's review packet mid-review. The design reviewer reads a packet for a different change and reports on work nobody asked about. review.sh also globs /tmp/PREFIX-*.png by mtime, so the other session's screenshots land in your captures.
design: Namespace by session or PID. review.sh's packet path is the one that matters most; the ready-cache and digest are cheap to regenerate but should still not be written from two places at once.
acceptance_criteria: Two simultaneous review.sh runs in one checkout produce two packets, neither overwriting the other.

title: dashboard: add, edit and close beads from the board
description:
The dashboard reports on the ledger but cannot touch it — verify_state's docstring states the principle outright ('the dashboard reports on the system, it doesn't drive it'), and for the gate that is right. For beads it isn't: the board is where you are already looking when you notice a bead is wrong, mis-titled, or done, and today that means switching to a terminal to say so. Filing a discovery the moment you see it is the whole premise of the ledger.

Wanted: create a bead from the board (title at minimum, ideally type/priority/parent), edit an existing one's title, priority and status, and close one with a reason.
design:
The write path already exists and should be followed rather than reinvented. Worktree actions POST to /worktree/<action> and validate the path against worktree_paths() — a path the request invented never reaches git. Run tasks POST to /run/<name> against the fixed TASKS table, so the only commands the server will ever run are the ones written in the file.

Bead edits want the same discipline: a fixed set of bd subcommands, and every id checked against the ids already in the current snapshot, so a request cannot name a bead the board isn't showing. Free text (title, close reason) is the one genuinely new thing — it reaches bd as an argument, so it must go through the argv list and never a shell.

Two smaller things: an edit must call touch() so the change lands on the next poll instead of waiting out the refresh, and writes contend with the refresher's own bd calls on the embedded Dolt lock — worth checking what a create does to the cadence while the board is polling.
acceptance_criteria: A bead can be created, retitled, reprioritised and closed without leaving the page, and the board reflects it on the next poll. No request can name a bead absent from the current snapshot, and no free text reaches a shell.

title: beads meant for a local model must carry their own spec
description: A small local model can execute a bead well only when the bead says what done looks like. Today most beads are a title and a paragraph, which is enough for a large model with the whole project in context and not enough for anything else. Without this the work-splitting in the model roster has nothing to split on.
design: Convention: a bead intended for a local agent carries --design and --acceptance filled in, plus a local-ok label. bd ready --label local-ok is the local queue. Documented in AGENTS.md, checked in bd preflight.
acceptance_criteria: AGENTS.md documents the convention; bd preflight flags a local-ok bead missing design or acceptance.
notes: Backend prerequisite is met: har-mjy fixed the opencode ollama provider, and all five local models now resolve.

title: harness-starter's own AGENTS.md is the boilerplate — the starter doesn't dogfood the fix
description: The root AGENTS.md is generic bd output: three overlapping beads blocks and a section about rm -i aliases. Nothing about the review pass, verify.sh, the ledger conventions, or that every real change goes in template/. An agent working on harness-starter from opencode would not know the one rule that matters most here.
acceptance_criteria: Root AGENTS.md is the installed template/AGENTS.md plus whatever is genuinely starter-specific.
close_reason: template/AGENTS.md ships as the harness contract, installed rather than pasted; add.sh wires CLAUDE.md to import it, collapses bd's three managed blocks to one in AGENTS.md, and strips the bd prime hook bd init re-registers. context.py tracks and counts AGENTS.md and fails on a stray block. Starter dogfooded. Review caught that bd init writes into AGENTS.md too — the first fix created the duplication it was removing, and the gate couldn't see it; also an unbounded sed range and a missing python3 guard. All fixed and verified on fresh installs.

title: staleness gate doesn't track CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md
description: The tracks:/context.lock gate watches HARNESS.md and three skills. The two files that actually tell an agent how to work are unwatched, which is why control-center-pro's AGENTS.md could sit as bd boilerplate through the entire project without anything noticing. HARNESS.md itself says staleness is the failure review can't catch; this is that failure, on the most load-bearing files in the repo.
acceptance_criteria: Both docs carry a tracks: comment and verify.sh fails when what they describe moves without them.
close_reason: template/AGENTS.md ships as the harness contract, installed rather than pasted; add.sh wires CLAUDE.md to import it, collapses bd's three managed blocks to one in AGENTS.md, and strips the bd prime hook bd init re-registers. context.py tracks and counts AGENTS.md and fails on a stray block. Starter dogfooded. Review caught that bd init writes into AGENTS.md too — the first fix created the duplication it was removing, and the gate couldn't see it; also an unbounded sed range and a missing python3 guard. All fixed and verified on fresh installs.

title: README and AGENTS.md never tell a project how its ledger reaches git
description:
A new install is never told how its beads ledger gets off the machine. bd dolt push/pull over refs/dolt/data is the transport, .beads/issues.jsonl is a passive export and not the source of truth, and nothing in the harness's own docs says either. The first person to clone a harnessed repo and find an empty ledger learns it the hard way.

Originally filed against CLAUDE.snippet.md, which no longer exists — har-jnz replaced it with template/AGENTS.md, installed rather than pasted. That is now the place this belongs: AGENTS.md's ledger section is where every agent in every tool reads about bd.
design: A short subsection under 'The ledger is beads' in template/AGENTS.md, plus a line in README's install section. Keep it to the two facts that matter: the transport is bd dolt push/pull, and the JSONL is an export nobody should treat as authoritative.
acceptance_criteria: A reader of the starter can state, without reading beads' source, how their ledger gets from their machine to their remote. If the managed beads block's refs/dolt/data claim cannot be corrected in place (it is rewritten by beads on upgrade), the harness's own docs say plainly what actually happens and that the managed block is wrong on this point.
notes: Found while diagnosing har-nqi: the wrong mental model from that block cost a real session's worth of debugging in control-center-pro.

title: add.sh reports success it never verified — 'initialised the ledger' can be a lie
description:
commands/add.sh:188 treats a zero exit from 'bd init --prefix $prefix' as the ledger being ready and prints 'initialised the ledger ($prefix-)'. It never checks that the ledger is actually usable or that the pieces the harness depends on exist. That is how control-center-pro reached a state where every session printed a healthy-looking brief while the ledger had no git-visible representation whatsoever.

The script already shows this instinct elsewhere and it pays off — the comment at :183 explains that keying on '.beads existing' would report an uninitialised ledger as initialised, 'which is how you find out later, one failing bd at a time'. That reasoning stops one step short: it validates that a prefix came back, not that the ledger works.

Compounding it: 'bd doctor', which is the tool that would normally catch a misconfigured ledger, refuses to run in embedded mode — it prints 'not yet supported in embedded mode' and exits. Embedded is what bd init produces by default, so the starter's projects are exactly the ones doctor cannot help.
design: Keep it to a couple of cheap assertions so install stays fast: 'bd stats' or 'bd list' returning cleanly, plus a grep for the export block once har-nqi lands. Do not shell out to bd doctor — it is unavailable in embedded mode, which is the default this installer produces.
acceptance_criteria: add.sh verifies the ledger after init — at minimum that a bead can be filed and read back, and that the configuration the harness relies on is present — and reports the real state rather than the exit code. A failed verification prints what to run to fix it.

title: design review can't see any hover state
description: scripts/dashboard.py shot photographs the page as it loads, so every capture the design reviewer ever reads is the default view. The dashboard puts real content behind hover and focus — the gate popover (which now holds a run button), the pulse tip, the lane stage tips, the file menu, the commit composer. None of it has ever been reviewed, and reviewer-design correctly refused to sign off on the run-button rework for exactly this reason: the only placement it could see was the empty one. Verified by hand on 2026-08-29 instead, driving the page in the browser pane, because the harness could not produce the captures. Wants 'shot' to take a list of states to photograph — an element to focus or hover before each capture — writing one /tmp/har-*.png per state so the packet carries them all.

title: dashboard: ledger_state spins up three Dolt engines per build
description: ledger_state in scripts/dashboard.py makes three separate bd calls — bd ready, bd list --all --limit 0, bd stale --days 14 — each spinning up its own embedded Dolt engine, together ~0.88s of a 2.5-3.1s state build. bd list --all already carries labels, description, design and notes; check whether ready-ness and staleness can be derived from that one payload instead of two more engine spin-ups. Diagnosed in control-center-pro as ccp-not.
notes: Partly addressed in a89d0ce: budget() was the bigger slice (1.75s of a 3.2s build) and is now on a 60s clock, taking builds to ~1.1s. What this bead was actually about is untouched — ledger_state still makes three bd calls (bd ready, bd list --all --limit 0, bd stale --days 14), ~1.1s, each its own Dolt engine.

title: dashboard: package as its own unit with a README
dashboard: panels vanish cleanly when their source is missing
description: No bd on PATH means no ledger lanes; no .claude/ means no harness panel; no verify logs means no gate. Absence as a first-class state, not an empty or confused shape. Root via git rev-parse --show-toplevel with a cwd fallback instead of the script's own path.

title: extract the dashboard as a standalone, adaptable package
notes: Hard requirement: dashboard is developed here and must update in place across every project that installed it. That makes 'shipped files are byte-identical everywhere' the load-bearing constraint — all per-project variation must live in a config file + runtime detection, never in edits to dashboard.py/index.html and never in install-time {{PROJECT}}/{{PREFIX}} substitution (dashboard.py:93,319,1048,1060,1079; index.html:6,1529 — all derivable at runtime). Then update = delete + re-copy, no merge. Needs a 'harness update' command; 'harness add' deliberately never overwrites (commands/add.sh:98).

title: dashboard backgrounds by default; portside alias in the announce
close_reason: default backgrounds via serve child; portside alias printed when the map matches port+directory

title: dashboard always opens in claude code's browser
close_reason: dashboard.py publishes launch.json + prints the pane instruction; no system browser path left

title: dashboard: two racing `up` calls both print 'started on 7391'
close_reason: fixed with the psymail backport: up now passes --port to the child that binds, and the bare path treats a failed bind as 'someone got here first' instead of asking holder() and acting on a stale answer. Both copies in step

title: self-host: finish the harness-starter install (CLAUDE.md, verify gate, seat, reviewer traps)
close_reason: self-hosted the starter: bin/harness frees the harness/ name the template needs, self-install guard removed, and the root now carries a working install with CLAUDE.md, a real gate (parse + probe-install + CLI), the Tern seat, and reviewer traps from this session. Review found the placeholder check passing vacuously when its own setup failed, and the *.md scope widening applied to the root copy but not the template — both fixed

title: consider shipping an optional code-graph skill — ask an index before opening files
description:
Lower-confidence idea from the same audit, filed so it isn't rediscovered.

control-center-pro carries an on-demand `graphify` skill: a local tree-sitter
code graph, no LLM, queried with explain/path instead of grepping and reading.
Measured 2026-09-01: `explain "CCPWidget"` returns 1.4KB naming all nine
related files with line numbers, against 58KB to read those files — 41x on the
question an agent actually asks. That is the single largest per-question saving
found anywhere in the audit, and it attacks the half of the bill that matters
(accumulated conversation), not the floor.

Two reasons it is not obviously starter material, and why this is P3:

- Language coverage. graphify is tree-sitter based and worked well on Swift,
  but a starter skill that silently produces a thin graph on some other
  language is worse than no skill.
- It is a dependency (`uvx --from graphifyy`) and an external tool the harness
  would then be quietly promising still works.

If it does ship, ship the trap with it: `graphify extract` given several paths
silently graphs only the FIRST one. The documented three-path line in CCP
produced a graph covering one module of three, which answered every question
about the other two with "not found" — a wrong answer that looks exactly like a
right one. One path plus a .graphifyignore is the working form.

The generic principle survives even if the tool doesn't: ask a cheap index
before opening files, and prefer a CLI that costs nothing until called over
anything that costs context every turn.
